raw_response:
Alright, let me think this through like the farmer I am.

---

I'm 37, got six mouths in the house counting me. My man works outside — factory, construction, wherever there's day-pay — so the land is mostly on me. My mother-in-law helps when her knees let her, and the kids pitch in on the weekends when school's not keeping them. I never went to school, but I've been in these fields since I was a little girl holding my grandma's hand at the edge of the wheat. I know this dirt. I know when it's thirsty, I know when the wheat looks peaked.

Ten mu and a bit. Not much. Everyone in our village does the same thing — wheat in winter, maize in summer, same as my mother, same as her mother. You don't mess with what works when you've only got ten mu. If I try something fancy and it fails, we eat less. Simple as that.

**Wheat, already in the ground since October.** I put down one bag of the mixed fertilizer — the 15-15-15, the one in the red sack — per mu when we sowed. That's what everyone does. One bag, no more, no less, because two bags would cost me another 130 yuan per mu and I just don't have it sitting around. When spring comes and the wheat turns green again, I'll top it up with some urea — maybe thirty jin or so per mu, a little less than some neighbors use because urea went up in price again this year. If the wheat looks yellow at jointing I'll give it a bit more, but I'll see what the field tells me.

Water — the well is there, electric pump, but the meter runs fast. I'll water three times: once when it comes out of dormancy around Qingming, once at jointing when it really needs a drink, and once when the grain is filling. Four times if it's a dry spring, but four times costs me real money. Seed I bought from the village co-op same as last year, a local strong-stalked variety, nothing fancy. Weeds I'll spray once in spring — the bottle from the agro shop, the one the shopkeeper points me to. Can't afford to pull ten mu of weeds by hand when my man isn't home.

**Maize after wheat.** Tight, tight window. The combine comes through in early June, and I have maybe five days to get the maize in before it's too late. I pay the village fellow with the no-till planter to come through — he charges 40 yuan a mu but he does it in one afternoon and I don't have to till. I drop a bag of compound fertilizer in with the seed through the planter. Seed has to be hybrid — I buy the yellow packet from the agro shop, whatever variety the shopkeeper says did well last year, costs about 60 yuan a mu. Around big trumpet stage when the maize is knee-high and looking hungry I side-dress urea. One watering usually, maybe two if July is dry. Maize takes less water than wheat because the summer rains come.

Last year I got about 420 jin of wheat per mu and a bit over 500 for maize. Same as the year before, give or take. This year I'm hoping for the same — no better, no worse. If the weather is kind, we'll be fine. If not, we'll manage like we always do.
